messages:
eva: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak i see a perf regression on long-seq workloads (seq_len >= 2k) on A100. p50 generation latency jumped and tokens/s dropped.
sam: ugh. which change exactly? the seqlen gating switch or the new warp-specialist path?
maria: i pulled the nightly perf report. perf-bot flagged it around 03:10 UTC.
perf-bot: nightly-bench: a100-longseq throughput: baseline 1100 toks/s -> current 920 toks/s (-16.4%). p50 latency 42ms -> 49ms. regression isolated to kernel variant 'smem_warp_opt_v3'.
eva: thanks @maria and @perf-bot. initial traces show lower SM occupancy on the winning kernel: 84% -> 62% at seqlen 2048. register spill rate up ~6% on that kernel.
ankur: does the kernel pick lower tile size or increase shared mem per thread? could be tilerouter selecting a bigger tile for cache locality which increases reg usage.
kai: i ran nvprof on a repro with batch=1, seqlen=2048. smem per block increased from 32KB -> 48KB in v3 path. register usage per thread goes 60 -> 78 regs. occupancy calc: with 78 regs and 48KB smem we get at most 2 blocks/SM vs 4 blocks/SM previously.
sam: that matches the occupancy drop. why did the picker choose bigger tile? config shows seqlen-aware policy now prioritizes tile splitting to reduce sharedmem bank conflicts. it chose tile_size=128->256 in the hot path.
maria: but doubling tile size reduced bank conflicts for shortseqs, but at longseq it's hurting because of reg pressure and fewer warps in flight.
eva: idea: add an occupancy constraint to the picker autotuner: prefer tile configs that keep occupancy >= 70% for the target device family unless latency wins significantly.
ankur: agree. maybe a scoring function: score = latency_est * alpha + (1/occupancy_penalty) * beta. tune alpha/beta per-device.
kai: i prototyped a quick filter: reject any candidate with expected active_warps < 32 for A100. that recovered tokens/s to ~1080 in a local run.
sam: nice. how did it affect bank conflicts? still acceptable?
kai: bank_conflict_rate slightly up (1.2% -> 1.6%) but overall throughput improved. no additional spills.
maria: we should also consider KV cache path: the seqlen-aware picker sometimes picks a prefetching scheme that increases per-thread state for KV (hoisting more prefetch buffers into registers) — that explains reg uptick.
eva: good catch. so two levers: (1) occupancy-aware filter, (2) KV prefetch budget per-thread cap. both in kernel-picker autotune.
ankur: can we add a quick perf test in PR gating? e.g., run microbench for seq_len [256,1024,2048] on an a100 smoke job and fail on >5% regression for any point.
sam: yes, but keep it lightweight. maybe a single batch-size profile and tokens/sec check.
perf-bot: perf-gate-suggestion: run jobs: a100-longseq (seq=2048,batch=1), a100-midseq (seq=1024,batch=2), check tokens/s delta vs baseline.json
maria: i'll add the occupancy filter and kv prefetch cap to the picker branch and push a WIP PR. will include the small perf job as a CI stage.
eva: assign to maria and kai for validation. @ankur can you draft the scoring formula and default thresholds for nvidia family?
ankur: on it. i'll post a short spreadsheet with expected occupancy/reg/smem tradeoffs.
kai: i'll run a small sweep on an a100 dev node tomorrow morning and post results here.
maria: thanks all. next steps: PR with changes + small CI perf job. if the perf gate passes, we'll merge and monitor nightly. tagging this thread for follow-ups.
eva: perfect. :thumbsup:
sam: one more note — log the kernel choice in production traces (tile_size, warp_specialist flag, kv_prefetch_budget) so we can correlate user regressions quickly.
maria: added to PR checklist.
perf-bot: noted. will surface kernel metadata in the next day of telemetry.
